domain: Identical StableHLO module, same selected PJRT client/device, three serial host-f64 executions

baselines.name: eaa executeStableHLO convenience API
baselines.citation: eaa54ba3 lib/backend/xla/xla_runtime.cpp executeStableHLO calls PjrtClient::compile and destroyExecutable once per invocation; three invocations imply three compile calls
baselines.basis: Source-derived operation count, not elapsed-time measurement

decision_points.name: compiled executable lifetime
decision_points.current_choice: compile and destroy inside each convenience call

alternatives.choice: explicit typed RAII program holding its originating PJRT session; caller compiles once and executes three times
alternatives.analytic_basis: Move compile outside the three-iteration execution loop. Exactly one explicit compile before loop replaces three convenience calls; all three execute/transfer paths remain, no implicit cache or host fallback. Program destroys executable once after final use.
alternatives.reported_effect: Calculated compile call reduction only; hardware compile cost and net wall-time gain unmeasured

predicted_delta.baseline_ref: source-derived eaa executeStableHLO compile once per call

alternatives.transferability_note: Authored decomposition; ICC ranks supplied mechanism, not independently derived speedup. Reuse valid only while module, client/session and device remain matching. Transfers/execution work unchanged. Real plugin/SDK/hardware confirmation unavailable.
alternatives.unmeasured_precondition: New typed reusable API not implemented yet. Preserve plugin/client/executable lifetime across runtime teardown/reinitialize; refuse wrong-owner execution.
alternatives.falsifying_experiment: Existing offline plugin-backed C++ wrapper control: three equal numerical executions with exactly one compile and one final executable destroy; baseline same three convenience executions compile3. Reject if any hidden recompilation, incorrect result, wrong-owner acceptance or teardown order failure. Counter receipt must distinguish offline control from physical device speed.
